title: REMOVAL OF NICKEL FROM AQUEOUS SOLUTIONS USING MULBERRY LEAVES AS A LOW-COST ADSORBENT
content:
REMOVAL OF NICKEL FROM AQUEOUS SOLUTIONS USING MULBERRY LEAVES AS A LOW-COST ADSORBENT

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Sarah Kareem Sahi and Batool Majid Saeed
Print ISSN : 2523-5664
Online ISSN : 2523-5672

Doi: 10.26480/wcm.01.2026.483.490

ABSTRACT

Water pollution by nickel cations poses a serious health and environmental risk, as its accumulation in the body through the food chain leads to respiratory illnesses, skin allergies, and kidney and liver disorders, in addition to being a potential carcinogen. It also negatively affects aquatic organisms even at low concentrations, causing inhibition of algae and fish growth and disruption of the ecological balance. Therefore, removing it from sewers and water bodies is extremely important due to its persistence and non-biodegradability. The present investigation aimed to check the feasibility of removing nickel cations using adsorption technique via mulberry leaves as a readily available and cost-effective adsorption medium in a batch adsorption unit under various operating conditions. The studied operating conditions range from 1 to 8, 100 to 500 rpm, 1 to 10 ppm, 0.5 to 12 g, and 20 to 50 °C, for pH, agitation speed, initial nickel cation concentration, adsorption dose, and temperature, respectively. The obtained results indicated that the removal efficiency was decline with increasing the initial concentration of nickel cations and temperature, while it was of similar changes to the other variables. Furthermore, 12 g of mulberry leaves achieved a maximum removal efficiency of approximately 80% of 10 ppm of nickel cations concentration, in neutral solution, after two hours of treatment at room temperature and an agitation speed of 400 rpm. FTIR analysis indicates that the adsorbent posses many active functional groups contribute significantly in adsorption of target ions. Moreover, the isotherm study show that the isotherm was favorable and well description by Langmuir isotherm model sue to the values of correlation coefficient and separation factors which were 0.9979, and 0.1061, respectively. By these results, it became possible to transform tree leaves from agricultural waste, which represents an environmental burden that must be disposed of, into a material of a useful application by converting them into an adsorption medium at a negligible cost.
